Title: Options failing to fetch should block PDF generation

Description:
### Description of the bug

If an option query fails, the PDF will just show the option value. Instead it should fail and let the user retry. Options are usually simple json files that rarely fail to fetch, however, apps can also implement option lists through code with any kind of external dependency which may fail for unkown reasons. In the browser normally this is not a huge issue, the layout will look a bit weird but the user can always refresh the page. But a PDF generated successfully is permanent, so we should not accept potentially saving incorrect data there.

https://github.com/Altinn/app-frontend-react/pull/3840#issuecomment-3502246948

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Instantiate an app with options and fill it out
2. Go to `?pdf=1`
3. Block the options request in browser dev tools
4. Summary should show the option value (not label) and readyForPrint is present

Title: VoiceOver (macOS) wcag issues for ImageUpload component

Description:
### Description of the bug

KS Digital discovered several WCAG-related issues when testing the new `ImageUpload` component using VoiceOver on Mac.

**(1) Focus is lost after selecting an image**
- After choosing a file, focus falls back to the browser window, not the component.
- VoiceOver navigation (`VO+Right`) stops working until manually pressing `Tab`.
- Expected behavior: focus should return to the Canvas where the image is displayed in the image upload component (similar to `FileUpload`).

**(2) Focus jumps to the top of the page when saving an image**
- When saving an uploaded image, focus moves to the top of the page rather than staying on the component.
- Expected behavior: After saving, focus should be on the delete button.

**(3) "Change Image" button has inconsistent focus**
- VoiceOver selects different parts of the button depending on direction of navigation:
   - Left to Right: selects icon
   - Right to left: selection text
- Likely caused by our current implementation where a hidden `<input type="file">` is linked to a `<label>` that is inside a `<Button asChild>`.
**This structure was originally chosen to support keyboard activation via space/enter, but it seems to cause unpredictable focus behavior in macOS screen reader.
```
<Input
  id={inputId}
  ref={fileInputRef}
  type='file'
  accept='image/*'
  onChange={handleImageChange}
  hidden
/>

<Button
  asChild
  data-size='sm'
  variant='secondary'
  data-color='accent'
  tabIndex={0}
  onKeyDown={(e) => handleFileSelectKeyDown(e)}
>
  <Label htmlFor={inputId}>
    <UploadIcon />
    <Lang id='image_upload_component.button_change' />
  </Label>
</Button>
```


### Steps To Reproduce

KS Digital demonstration (VoiceOver on Mac):

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/00750720-b387-4968-9cec-d23c72d34415

Correct behavior in FileUpload:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f7bc2884-182a-4ea7-816a-927820789dcd

### Additional Information

There is a Slack thread with additional context (in locked channel).
Let me know if you want access or have any other questions:
https://digdir-samarbeid.slack.com/archives/C090VFARF1V/p1761046046934189

Title: Adding object to group does not verify leaf types in data model

Description:
### Description of the bug

The 'save to group' functionality merged in #3236 shows a problem with the `FD.useAppendToList()` hook it uses to store an object in the data model. While the regular 'FD.useSetLeafValue()' hook will convert the data type (to, for example, a number when a numeric type is specified in the schema file), the `FD.useAppendToList()` hook does not. This can cause a hard crash when for example combined with `Checkboxes` that uses a numerical option list. Since all options are converted to strings, the string will carry into the object stored in the data model, which may be defined as taking a numerical value (not a string). 

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Check out `ttd/component-library` commit f3e15048ea77d42561937c872fb479518ada69f5
2. Go to the checkboxes page
3. Scroll down and check one of the checkboxes
4. Observe that frontend crashes when getting a 500 from the backend

Title: Navigering mellom hovedskjema og underskjema (valideringer)

Årsregnskap har et par skjemaer hvor det er valideringer i underskjema som baserer seg på verdier i felter fra både hovedskjema-datamodellen og underskjema-datamodellen. Per i dag kjøres disse basert på GenericFormDataValidator i backend.

I ettertid har vi sett at akkurat disse valideringene "henger noe igjen" i brukergrensesnittet gitt endring av verdier i hovedskjema (verdier som valideringene baserer seg på), når man navigerer frem og tilbake mellom hovedskjema og underskjema. Legger ved eksempel på dette (Steps to reproduce). 

Har testet en alternativ løsning - å bytte interface fra GenericFormDataValidator til IValidator med bruk av IInstanceDataAccessor, men vi ser at denne løsningen har samme utfordring ved at valideringer «henger igjen».

Har testet PATCH-requester ifb. Oppdateringer av felter i skjema, og disse kjører som forventet (hvilke/antall valideringer som er aktuelle vises som forventet i requestene).

Et videre spørsmål er om dette går på en oppdatering i frontend i overgang mellom underskjema og hovedskjema - håper noen kan teste hos dere? For å se om dere får gjenskapt samme problemstilling. Det funker å fjerne/vise valideringene ved refresh.

Title: PDF generation fails (`pdfLayoutName` config issue)

Description:
### Description of the bug
Frontend version [4.17.2](https://github.com/Altinn/app-frontend-react/releases/tag/v4.17.2) introduced stricter PDF layout name validation, which caused previously functional apps to start malfunctioning. The only deployed app we have found to be susceptible to this issue, is [dmf/drift-rapport](https://altinn.studio/repos/dmf/drift-rapport).

The nature of this issue results in a silent error, where the PDF is indeed generated without any detectible issues, but it does not contain any data.

Its difficult to pin down exactly how to classify this issue. On one hand, the old versions of frontend allowed misconfigured apps to somehow function, which in itself can be described as a bug. On the other hand, since it "was already working", fixing the issue can be seen as a breaking change.

As for mitigation, the service owners of the affected app have already fixed their configuration, so there's no hotfix or anything required from the app-frontend-react side of things. However, there are a number of submitted instances of the app which are now lacking PDF data.

[Slack thread](https://digdir.slack.com/archives/C0760NPT2BE/p1740658933273769)

### Steps To Reproduce
1. Find or make an app that makes use of `pdfLayoutName`
2. (Mis)configure the value to be a string array instead of a string
3. Render PDF
   - Using frontend versions < 4.17.2, the PDF renders fine
   - Using frontend versions >= 4.17.2, the PDF contains only headers and is otherwise blank 

### Related issues
- https://github.com/Altinn/app-frontend-react/issues/648

### Interventions
- https://github.com/Altinn/app-frontend-react/pull/3062
- https://github.com/Altinn/app-lib-dotnet/pull/1146

Title: Map-component fails on first render when geometry array contains one singular Point WKT

Description:
### Description of the bug

When map-component recieves an array of geometries in WKT format from datamodel, it renders the geometries with labels on the map.
If the geometry array only contains one geometry of type Point, it will fail on first render. 
If the page and map has loaded before the Point is put into the geometry array, then it renders the Point on the map properly. It only fails if there is one singular Point in the geometry array from datamodel before the page has loaded, and before the map has finished its initial render.

Process:
Puts one Point WKT in the geometry array, and then loads the page with Map.

Expected behavior:
Map loads properly and shows a marker for the Point.

Actual behavior:
Map fails and page shows an error describing invalid lat lng values given to the Map.



### Steps To Reproduce

1. Create an app
2. Add mapComponent to layout
3. Create an array for geometries in datamodel with structure `{label: string, data: string}`

6. Add one singular object to the geometry array in datamodel (ex: `label: "35", data: "POINT (6.39786261469293 62.4839094223067)"` )

Example mapcomponent config:
```json
{
  "id": "kartvisning",
  "type": "Map",
  "textResourceBindings": {
    "title": "Map"
  },
  "dataModelBindings": {
    "geometries": "Geometries"
  },

}
```

Title: App gets stuck on instantiation after switching party

Description:
### Description of the bug

If you instantiate an app, then go back to party selection and select a different party, you will see an infinite loader with `reason='instantiating'`. The reason is the following check:
```ts
const shouldCreateInstance = !!party && !instantiation.lastResult && !instantiation.isLoading;
```
This check fails due to `instantiation.lastResult` being truthy, probably because we already created an instance with a different party before.

It may also be prevented by the implementation of the `instantiate` function:
```ts
if (instantiate.data || instantiate.isPending || instantiate.error || isInstantiatingRef.current) {
  return;
}
```

Title: Geometry in map component not updating when changed

Description:
### Description of the bug

The map-component renderes geometries given to it by the datamodel. The component expects an array of objects `{ data: string; label?: string; }`.
When objects are added to the array, the map component renderes them properly. On the other hand, if you change the data/polygon part of a geometry that has previously been rendered on the map, the map moves to the new geometry location, but the geometry itself remains unchanged. Since the map moves to the new placement, that means the geometry bounds are recalculated, showing that the datamodel has been updated correctly. It seems like this happens as long as the data/gemoetry object has the same index and label in the datamodel array as it had on previous renders/updates. Reversing the list in the app before storing it in the datamodel so the index of the object has been changed since last update makes the geometry behave correctly/as expected.

The problem is propably with the key of the geojson components in the map component. 
```ts
{geometries?.map(({ data, label }, i) => (
        <GeoJSON
          key={`${i}-${label}`}
```

### What happened
Geometry is placed in datamodel and rendered in map. When the geometry is changed in the datamodel, the geometry remains in place on the map, instead of moving where it should.

### What should have happened
Map should have moved to the new placement of the geometry, and the geometry object should have moved and adapted to the changed geometry data.






### Steps To Reproduce

1. Make an app with a map and geometries that can be changed by the user.
2. Place geometries in the datamodel/map
3. Watch them render on the map
4. Change/update the data prop/field of one of the geometries
5. The map should move the view to the updated placement of the geometry, while the geometry stays in place.

Title: Schema validation coerces missing numbers to 0

Description:
### Description of the bug

Slack: https://altinn.slack.com/archives/C02EJ9HKQA3/p1730302631757679

We use `coerceTypes: true` in AJV, this will convert values to the "correct" type before validating. This can be useful if e.g. a number is stored as a string, so that `"12"` will be treated as `12` and will not fail the `type: number` validation. A less fortunate side-effect of this is that it will also coerce `null` to something that is valid for each type. For numbers, `null` -> `0`, which can cause validations to appear when they should not. We use `null` to say that a value is missing, and this should not give an error unless it is `required`.

`coerceTypes: true` was probably necessary previously when we stored all of the form data as strings. This is no longer the case, so we may be able to get rid of this option now. It could easily break things however, so we cannot just remove this without testing extensively in existing apps.

One possible solution is removing `null` values from the datamodel before running the schema validation. It does not seem like we can fix this by messing with other AJV options (`useDefaults: 'empty'` did not change things)

Title: Description on radio and checkbox group is not connected to the `fieldset`

Description:
### Description of the bug

SSB has reported that the description text (under Legend) is not connected to anything. This means that it wont be read by a screen reader when entering the radio/checkbox group when you are using a screen reader. 

One solution is to handle it the same way we do in our design system or Gov uk where you use an aria-describedby on the `<fieldset>`element. This will work with JAWS and NVDA. (Not VoiceOver)

The other solution is to not handle this at all as NAV Aksel has done and not use any aria-describedby. The screen reader user needs to find this information going to the element themselves. As of now `aria-describedby`is technically allowed on `fieldset` but there are no documentation on what that means. How should it behave? Because this is not defined in any way screen reader support is not optimal. But VoiceOver is the only that has not supported this in any way it seems. 

I would recommend going for the first solution here in short term as it is better then nothing. We will investigate this in another task in designsystemet to see if there are any other way to convey extra information in a fieldset context.



### Steps To Reproduce

Go to an app with a radio/checkbox group (with description) And test it with a screen reader

Title: Suboptimal oppførsel ved levering av undersøkelse under høy last på systemet

Description:
### Description of the bug

Dersom systemet overbelastes og det feiler ved levering av undersøkelse på grunn av overbelastning, så er det ikke optimal håndtering av denne situasjonen.

Ved høy last (eksempelvis tilsvarende trykk 40.000 / 1 time, eller 6666/10minutter) feiler det for enkelte ved levering: "_Ja, jeg er ferdig_"-knappen blir slik den skal grået ut med en spinner over, men ingenting skjer deretter: Knappen blir stående grå å spinne, og ingenting blir levert. Ventet til lenge etter den høye trafikken ga seg, og den ble stående, og sjekk i mottak viste at eleven ikke hadde levert.

Deretter, dersom bruker frisker opp siden, blir lever-knappen aktiv, og bruker kan deretter klikke lever, og den kan da gå OK. Så en oppmerksom bruker kan komme rundt dette, og få levert, men faren er at flere elever i en slik situasjon vil anta at "_det sikkert gikk greit_", og logge ut eller ikke gjøre noe mer, og at det potensielt ikke blir meldt fra til support om dette, og undersøkelse heller ikke blir levert.

En bedre oppførsel i en slik situasjon hvis levering først skal feile, kan være at det vises en feilmelding om at "_Besvarelsen kunne ikke leveres, vent 1 minutt og forsøk lever-knapp igjen_". Det er ikke gitt at en elev frisker opp siden for å klikke lever på nytt om noe sånt her skjer.

Merk at dette altså er ved høy last der responstider i systemet trolig er 10+ sekunder . Så det er snakk om hvordan systemet oppfører seg ved overbelastning. 

-------
Ved nærmere undersøkelse av nettverksloggen i nettleseren så viser det seg at i tilfeller dette oppstår så dukker ikke PUT-request mot "/process/next" opp i det hele tatt ved klikk på "Ja, jeg er ferdig" (Se vedlagt video) på "additional information"
Da er det kanskje noe feil i modellen? Og feilmeldingen kan gis på et tidligere tidspunkt? Har ikke sett nærmere på dette.

### Steps To Reproduce

Kjør en hard ytelsestest på systemet, med for eksempel et trykk på 10k elever i løpet av 15 minutter som gjennomfører. Logg samtidig manuelt inn i nettleser og klikk på siste lever-kallet. Det er ikke konsekvent at dette skjer, så forvent å kanskje måtte forsøke et par ganger..
Ta kontakt for bistand til å starte en ytelsestest samtidig, og/eller testdata for innlogging.

### Additional Information

Videorecording av skjerm.
I tilfeller der det fungerer OK så dukker PUT-kall opp ved klikk på grønn "Ja jeg er ferdig knapp", men som video viser dukker ikke det opp her ved høy belastning:

Title: URL til skjema under utfylling gjenoppretter ikke alltid tilstanden.

Description:
### Description of the bug

Vi har kommet over to ulike situasjoner der en URL til et skjema som er under utfylling ikke fører brukeren fram til skjemaet, eller tilstanden under utfylling ikke er den samme som da man forlot skjemaet.

1) Når man følger en lenke til et skjema men ikke er innlogget
Når man følger en lenke til et skjema, men av ulike årsaker ikke lenger er innlogget så vil man først bli logget inn, deretter velger man part man representerer og så går man inn i et nytt skjema. 

2) Når man går inn i et skjema og er innlogget og representerer en part
Når man følger en lenke til et skjema under utfylling, men man representerer en annen part enn den parten man representerte da man fyllte ut skjema, så vil man fortsatt representere den parten man representerte før man åpnet skjemaet. Det kan føre til at man sender inn skjemaet som en part (den man var logget inn som da man gjenåpnet skjemaet) med data om en annen part (den man valgte da man startet utfyllingen av skjema)

I begge tilfeller ville jeg forventet at når man åpner en url til et skjema, vil det fremstå eksakt slik man forlot det, selv om man må logge på eller har en annen kontekst (representerer en annen part), kanskje også vise den siden/prosess-steget man sto på sist.

Mer kontekst: https://altinn.slack.com/archives/C02EJ9HKQA3/p1727253108947259

### Steps To Reproduce

Start utfylling av et skjema
Kopier lenken til skjema
Åpne  et nytt anonymt browservindu.
Kopier inn lenken.
Logg inn.
- man har nå opprettet et nytt skjema -
Kopier lenke
Bytt part man representerer
Lim inn lenke til opprinnelig skjema
Man representerer fortsatt parten man byttet til, ikke parten man representerte da man opprette første skjema.

Title: Subform patch issue

Description:
### Description of the bug

Reported via [Slack](https://altinn.slack.com/archives/C02EJ9HKQA3/p1726058566919759):

Creation of subform data element succeeds, but the subsequent prefill (`preselectedOptionIndex`) appear to produce multiple PATCH requests to the backend. Resulting in failed preconditions.

This bug is present if the current page is rendering a subform component, or if we are inside a subform routing context.
A `preselectedOptionIndex` on a radio button in the main form, on a page that contains a subform table, results in the same bug.

### Steps To Reproduce

0. Checkout the latest [feature/subform](https://github.com/Altinn/app-frontend-react/tree/feature/subform) branch
1. Clone https://altinn.studio/repos/brg/aarsregnskap-vpfo-202405/src/branch/testing_to_underskjema
2. In the file `App/ui/Underskjema/layouts/01layout.json` insert the following property for component `U-01-Radiobuttons-Regnskapstype`:
   ```json
   "preselectedOptionIndex": 1
   ```
3. Run the app and the local frontend code
4. Create a new instance of the app with the following authentication: `Cayman Islands VPFO (Organisation)`. If asked to confirm which actor you wish to instantiate the form as, select `VPFO` again
5. On the first page in the main form, towards the top, click the big `+` button in the subform table
6. Observe the network stack as the subform loads

### Additional Information

The data model value associated with `U-01-Radiobuttons-Regnskapstype` (`Rapport-RR0007U.aarsregnskap.type.value`) sends a PATCH request to the server three times. Each request believes the previous value for the field was `empty`, which is correct for the first request but incorrect for the subsequent ones.

The form itself also seems to re-render three times during load, which could perhaps be related to this bug.

The re-render issue can be observed at any time, by simply refreshing the page.

Source: https://github.com/Altinn/app-frontend-react/issues/2071 State: CLOSED Labels: kind/bug Title: ListComponent fails to identify selected row if one of the columns is not `string` Description: ### Description of the bug If one of the columns in a datalist is not a string, f.ex. an int, and this value is saved to the data model through the ListComponent's dataModelBindings. It will never show any row as selected, even if the form data gets populated when a row is clicked. This is because currently, the list component gets its form data casted to string, and compares this with the data in the raw dataList rows, which could contain other types (like integers). Title: Schema validation does not work with `-` in datamodel path

Description:
### Description of the bug

A field with a `-` in the datamodel path will not get any schema validations. This seems to be due to an edge-case in the `jsPropertySyntax` we get from `Ajv` which is not handled correctly.

Working example:
Path: `Oppgave.rapporteringsenhet.kontaktperson.epost_1`
Instance path from Ajv: `.Oppgave.rapporteringsenhet.kontaktperson.epost_1`
Result: `Oppgave.rapporteringsenhet.kontaktperson.epost_1`

Buggy example:
Path: `Oppgave.rapporteringsenhet.e-post`
Instance path from Ajv: `.Oppgave.rapporteringsenhet["e-post"]`
Result: `Oppgave.rapporteringsenhete-post`

This can be fixed either by fixing the `processInstancePath()` function on `jsPropertySyntax` or switching to using `jsonPointer` and using a new parsing method. (`jsPropertySyntax` has been deprecated in `Ajv` for some time anyways)

Title: Inconsistent Language Display in AddressComponent

Description:
### Description of the bug

Currently, the AddressComponent labels in some scenarios display the incorrect language. This occurs because the address component relies on the language set in the end user's Altinn profile. 
Consequently, the Altinn 3 app may display the wrong language in the AddressComponent text labels when the selected language in the user's profile is not supported by the specific App. This issue extends to cases where application supports languages other than Bokmål, Norwegian Nynorsk, and English, resulting in incorrect language display.

![image](https://github.com/Altinn/app-frontend-react/assets/75472603/73ad3f84-6464-4fec-9002-bfac42f22364)

To address this issue, implementing the following solutions may solve the problem:

1. Language Control: The AddressComponent should be controlled by the language selected within the application rather than relying on the language set in the end user's Altinn profile. This ensures consistent language display regardless of the user's profile settings.

2. Customizable Text Labels: Provide developers with the ability to customize the text labels of the address component using language files. This flexibility allows developers to tailor the text labels according to the specific language requirements of their application.

1. Log on to tt02 and set the langue to English.

Title: IAppOptionsProvider does not provide options if "mapping" field is never set

### Description of the bug

However, there are ways to fill out this form without ever filling out the DEPENDENCY FIELD, and when you do that the DYNAMIC FIELD will just be stuck with a loading icon. The code in the `IAppOptionsProvider` can handle this value not being set, but it is never run during a regular filling out of the form if you do not fill out the DEPENDENCY FIELD. 

What I want is for the `IAppOptionsProvider` to run when the form is first loaded in, even though the DYNAMIC FIELD is hidden at this point. I'm almost sure this has worked before, but I couldn't say when.

1. Create a List with four fields in the data model: "isDependency" (bool), "dependencyPercentage" (string), "isDynamic" (bool) and "dynamicPercentage" (string). Make all RadioButtons inside a Repeating Group. (Repeating Group POSSIBLY not needed)

4. Select "No" on "isDependency", select "Yes" on "isDynamic". 
5. Observe that the option for "dynamicPercentage" is just stuck on loading, since "dependencyPercentage" was never called.

Title: Summary/PDF - rendered before dynamic options are loaded

Description:
### Description of the bug

In the context of implementing Tanstack Query in useGetOptions and PDF, we've identified a bug that occurs in certain scenarios where options are not fully loaded/fetched before they are displayed in the PDF or Summary. 

This issue is primarily associated with dynamic options, which do not appear to finish loading before they are rendered in PDF or Summary. It has been observed by @bjosttveit that the `initiallyLoaded` variable within `useAllOptions` is being set to true before it has actually finished loading. This was done by wrapping the reducer of `allOptions`, enabling it to log the state of `initiallyLoaded` for each update. 

![image](https://github.com/Altinn/app-frontend-react/assets/74791975/8e2e1598-e3ba-437f-861c-6653fd355d39)



### Steps To Reproduce

Here's an example to reproduce this issue:
1. Start the frontend test app in the `changeName` form.
2. Reduce the network speed (I set it to d: 200kb/s, u: 200kb/s and latency: 4000ms).
3. Refresh the page
4. In the drop-down lists under "Referanser", change the option in source, then quickly navigate to the summary page.
5. You will probably notice that "Referanse2" hasn't had enough time to fetch before the summary is rendered. It should display the same value as Referanse.
![image](https://github.com/Altinn/app-frontend-react/assets/74791975/a271bec7-3bb9-4c9d-9892-bab7a417aad1)

6. If you refresh the page while on the summary page, the issue won't resolve itself. To fix this, you need navigate back to `form` so that these dynamic options can finish rendering. After that, navigate back to the summary page again.

This task includes:

Title: Tech debt: Language support

Description:
Right now, our language support is in a bit of a sad state:
- Ideally, variables in text resources should work everywhere, automatically, even with lookups inside repeating groups. They don't, because we rely on complex rewriting of text resource bindings on components for this to work (and it only works on one level of repeating groups).
  - See #1185 
  - See #1191 
  - See the tests that were introduced, but disabled in #1217
- Ideally, looking up data model paths using variables should work without using `[{0}]` index placeholders, as we have tools for resolving the data model path relative to the currently rendered `LayoutNode` (see `transposeDataModel`). We should remove these index placeholders from the text resources.
- We should not have to maintain stuff like `replaceTextResourcesSaga`, this should happen automatically when looking up a language/text key.


Done (as of #1255):
- ~~We have loads of functions used for similar things, many of which are deprecated and should be removed (replace with `useLanguage`):~~
  - `getLanguageFromKey`
  - `getTextResourceByKey`
  - `getParsedLanguageFromKey`
  - `getTextFromAppOrDefault`
- ~~Only the last one of these fall back to our so-called 'app language', the integrated list of text keys.~~
- ~~Ideally, every text key in our own collection should be possible to override using the supplied app text resources.~~

Title: Validating an active row in repeating group can be interrupted

Description:
### Description of the bug

Validation of an active row is interrupted if user interacts with other elements that triggers an action. With the [new feature](https://github.com/Altinn/app-frontend-react/pull/1071) this bug can cause that ``isLoading`` is kept as ``true`` (add-button is disabled).
User can “restart” the validation by clicking again on the “save and close”-button of the active row. 
A worse scenario is if the user chooses to delete the active row during validation and this is the only row. The solution then is to refresh the page to re-enable the add button. 

Not sure what steps should be taken to solve this, but a possible solution could be to disable other elements while validating the active row, or have the disabled add button is re-enabled if the validation is interrupted.


### Steps To Reproduce

1. Go to an app that has the component "repeating group" and set ``"alwaysShowAddButton": true`` [See docs. ](https://docs.altinn.studio/app/development/ux/fields/grouping/alternatives/)
2. Open a new row with validation as a trigger, e.g. ``"triggers": ["validateRow"]``
3. Click on the "save and close"-button and while this is validating click on a different element that triggers a new action. Such as open a row in the "reference group" from the frontend-test app.

Title: Showing components with "triggers": ["validation"] causes a storm of validation on server

Description:
### Description of the bug

For some reason it was decided to do single field validations for all components that are newlyVisible in order to ensure that validation errors that **only** appear on single field validation is restored after a component has been temporarily hidden.

https://github.com/Altinn/app-frontend-react/blob/ee041858cd282908b7d2c96150a75ba648ac9952/src/features/form/dynamics/conditionalRendering/conditionalRenderingSagas.ts#L88-L106

This is code that comes from
*  https://github.com/Altinn/app-frontend-react/pull/627

In some of our schemas we have a few pages that are initially invisible, but gets visible after the user makes a selection on the first page. Calling `/validate` tens of times is somewhat problematic for performance, but the obviously worse part is that these newly visible fields almost certainly isn't valid (as they are empty), so the user will have lots of errors on pages they have not even visited yet.

My suggestion would be to just remove this loop over newly visible components. We currently clear and never restore these errors on page refresh anyway, so as a developer, you can't rely on these errors being restored 

An alternaltive would be to check if the components with `"triggers": ["validation"]` is empty before triggering the validation.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Create an app with 2 pages.
2. Make the second page conditionally hidden based on a radio button on page 1
3. Add a 3 components with `"triggers": ["validation"]` on page 2

Open devtools and see that `/validate` is called 3 times when the radio button on page 1 is toggled to show page 2.

Title: Frontend does not ignore `required` validations from backend

Description:
### Description of the bug

Apps that enable `"RemoveHiddenDataPreview"` gets the benefit of backend validation of components that are marked `"required": true` (or an expression that evaluates to true). This is great because it ensures that users that open devtools, or deliver schema using the API, also is forced to answer all the required questions before submitting.

A problem is that backend during validation does not know what language the user wants their messages, so it can't really say anything more than `required` and indicate the field and component that triggered the error. I suggest to improve it somewhat in https://github.com/Altinn/app-lib-dotnet/pull/217, but as frontend already generates great warnings for empty required fields, the result will always be a duplicated validation message. I think the best solution is to just ignore any validation error with `"code": "required"` so that frontend can handle required independent of backend. (there probably need to be some way to show the error in case frontend thinks the instance is OK, but backend still thinks required values are missing).

 
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/131616/228529065-507fbd09-5467-4cf9-bf15-2e756dfbd2cc.png)

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Enable `"RemoveHiddenDataPreview"`
2. Add components with `"required"` to the schema
3. Trigger validation with empty required components
4. See that you get double error messages for required where one just states `TODO required`

Title: WCAG: Tab order is wrong in repeating group v2

Description:
### Description of the bug

This is related to issue #908 where the overall issue was fixed, but with additional scenarios the focus would stop working as intended. This is related to how the HTML is constructed for repeating groups. 

The repeating group container consists of a table of rows. Each row represents a group. New groups is added above the "add new group"-button. Hence the tab order doesn't visit the new group, but continues its path below.

So, the current workaround for #908, is to shift the focus upwards to the first focusable element in the edit container of the new group - using useRef and useEffect.

However, if the reference group is open and we then also opening a repeating group, the focus would be on reference instead of repeating. The reason for this is that both groups are rendered (reference is re-rendered when repeating is opened). And since reference is further down in the HTML DOM it will result in useRef using reference group as ref when the logic of focus is executed in useEffect. Ref. Video 1.

A similar issue occurs if we navigate back and forth in the edit container of repeating group. The focus will stop working as intended because it is no longer focused on the top element. Ref. Video 2.

We could have added more conditional statements to deal with these scenarios before executing the logic to shift focus. However, this would not be easy to work with in the long run.

A possible solution (in the short run?) is to move the buttons up in the HTML DOM so that new groups added are below them, but visually displayed as they are above. Here I also refer to the navigation buttons in the edit container of a repeating group. This would make it easier to deal with issues on the WCAG tab order.

In the longer run we may consider investing in an overall restructuring of repeating groups (and also group container?). 

**Update from UU test by SSB**
When pressing "Lagre og åpne neste" focus is moved to the previous "rediger" button. Focus should be on first field in the group. And if you press "Lagre og lukk" focus should be on "rediger" on the same row.

Maybe some of theese issues will be fixed if we decide to go trough with this issue: https://github.com/Altinn/app-frontend-react/issues/1630
Making it a modal and locking the tab order inside the modal should be easier to control focus than opening up all of the tables.

Title: role: alert when info-panel is used with dynamics

Description:
### Description of the bug
We have some situations today where apps use our panel component in combination with dynamics to create an alert component that triggers based on user input. This gives us an accessebility issue where this panel should have an aria alert role so that screen readers also can get this information.

## conundrum
We cant just add an alert role on our panels because: 

> The most important thing to know about the alert role is that it's for content that is dynamically displayed, not for content that appears on page load.
[Source ](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Roles/alert_role)

One of the main uses for the panel component is to highlight information on a page, and is often used so that is visible on page load. We need to seperate dynamic alerts and those that is only used to highlight static information.

Also, this is pretty similar to our soft-validation functionality. If we expand the functionality of our panels to handle this, we have to seperate components doing almost the same thing. This might be hard to comunicate the difference between the 2. 

One solution is to in some way expand the soft validation so that it meets our appdevelopers needs. Then we can contain this to one consept that is easier to communicate. The other is to add some attribute to the panel that can be set by the app-developer when they use it with dynamics, but then we add alert functionality to a component that maybe should be used as a way of presenting static information, and by having another attribute the app-developer has to worry about, we increase the chance of accessebility issues in apps that use this feature. 

Or maybe a developer have a better suggestion on how to solve this? 😇

Small example: 
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/33222679/226847850-41460207-0e00-4e74-a730-8816e0c60f57.png)

[aria alert documentation](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Roles/alert_role)


## Specification
The documentation specifies that you need to be careful with the use of alert as it can be very intrusive for screen reader users. Is there a risk that it might be overused, should the developer be able to turn it of if the information is not that important. 
- [ ] Look at relevant cases
- [ ] Define guidelines
- [ ] Added to all variants (info, success and warning)
- [ ] Consider adding the alert that is specified in the designsystem [Issue](https://github.com/digdir/designsystem/issues/78)

### Steps To Reproduce

Go to an app with soft validation and test if it is read by the screen reader when it is triggered.

Title: UiConfig page settings are sticky

Description:
### Description of the bug

There are currently two places that page settings can be set, layout-sets and settings.json and these both set page settings using the `updateCommonPageSettings` function. It is not actually defined in the layout-sets schema.

The problem is that if you set a setting like `showLanguageSelector` to true in one layout-set, and leave it undefined in the next layout set, the setting will not be reset when navigating to the next process step even though it is implicitly false when undefined. A refresh will reset the setting. This happens because `updateCommonPageSettings` uses the existing value if the new value is undefined.

I suppose the settings in the layout-sets file are "global" for all process steps, and the expected behaviour is that settings.json should override layout-sets settings if defined, and be set to false if undefined in both places.

Title: Datepicker: Duplicate validation on `"triggers": ["validation"]`

Description:
### Description of the bug

When using Datepicker in combination with `"triggers": ["validation"]`, we seem to send the data for validation on server even in cases where we know the date format is not valid yet. When the data model has been set up with `xsd:date` as the type, the generated C# class contains a regex the date needs to match - but as the data is invalid, the regex does not match, and we get a generic error back from the server complaining about the data not matching a regex. This error is not meaningful for users:

![birthdate-validation-regex](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/700139/214005412-106da790-7959-4167-b613-057e4538bf89.png)

We should probably automatically ignore this specific regex validation message for datepicker fields, thus making sure full page (or all-page) validation still works as expected (even when the datepicker field has not been filled completely).

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Set up a Datepicker
2. Add `"triggers": ["validation"]` on it
3. Bind it to a location in the data model using `xsd:date`
4. Observe it showing the regex in the validation message when filling out the date

Title: Nested repeating group is not visible when `largeGroup=false`

Description:
### Description of the bug

Currently, when using `largeGroup: false` (default) on a summary of a repeating group, any nested repeating groups will be hidden. This is because there is no string representation of a repeating groups data. Previously it would actually show the field with an empty value but this was removed due to confusion.

When using `largeGroup: true` the nested group will be displayed as a "compact" group.

Not sure how these kinds of summaries should be handled. Should nested groups be hidden from summary? Show just the number of elements? Is there some possible string representation of a repeating group? Or, should it show all of the content in a compact way?

A problem currently is that PDF generation uses `largeGroup: false` by default when using automatic PDF generation (not using a custom layout), and there is currently no way of overriding summary props using this method. This means that if you have a nested repeating group that you want to be visible in the PDF you are forced to make an entire custom layout. I would like to avoid making `largeGroup: true` default, as it takes up a lot more space and is not generally what is needed for most repeating groups.

This needs design work before it can be implemented.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Create a repeating group containing a nested repeating group.
2. Create a summary for the first group, using `largeGroup: false`.
3. Fill inn information in both the first and nested repeating group.
4. Observe that the data for the nested repeating group is not present.

Title: Validation of `multipleOf` keyword with decimals fails sporadically

Description:
### Description of the bug

When validation against a schema like
```json
{
    "properties": {
      "test": {
        "type": "number",
        "multipleOf": 0.1,
      }
    }
}
```

The validation fails on valid numbers. F.ex. here, where `multipleOf: 0.1` should result in `855,8` being a valid number.

![image (4)](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1636323/207308087-b1a889ae-2621-4290-bb71-5562b7dcd8db.png)

In addition, we are missing standard text for the validation error message for `multipleOf` keyword.


### Steps To Reproduce

1. Go to an app and modify the data model so that one of the fields has the `multipleOf` keyword set to `0.1` (for `type: number` fields).
2. Type some different numbers into the field: `1.1`, `1.2`,  `1.3`, etc, and see that some of them will result in a validation error.

### Additional Information

This seems to be a known rounding issue, see https://github.com/ajv-validator/ajv/issues/652.
It can be fixed either by specifying an option `multipleOfPrecision` to the validator, or by re-implementing that keyword with our own method.

Title: `SummaryGroupComponent` shows non-existing validation errors

Description:
### Description of the bug

If there are validation errors on a group, the respective summary component shows a message like this:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/47412359/204753515-201c5f1e-17e5-469b-8e46-055661d87d28.png)
The problem is that the way it checks for validation errors in the group is wrong, and can potentially say that there are validation errors when there are in fact none. This is because it only checks whether the component-key exists in the validations stored in redux, it does not check if it has an `error`-array with `length > 0`, which is the way the group-component itself checks if it contains errors.

This is the logic currently used in the `SummaryGroupComponent`:

```typescript
if (pageRef && componentIdWithIndex && validations[pageRef] && validations[pageRef][componentIdWithIndex]) {
  groupErrors = true;
}
```

`RepeatingGroupTable` uses the more correct function `componentHasValidations` from `validation.ts` to check for validations in it's children, this does a more comprehensive check:

```typescript
return Object.keys(validations[layoutKey]?.[componentId] || {})?.some((bindingKey: string) => {
    const length = validations[layoutKey][componentId][bindingKey]?.errors?.length;
    return length && length > 0;
  });
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Start a new instance in the `frontend-test` app.
2. Navigate to the `group` layout set
3. Do not add prefill elements
4. Add a new row in the repeating group, and fill in some data in the nested group on the second multi-page
5. Save the row, and observe that there are no validation errors
6. Go to summary and see an error message for the nested group

In the redux store, there are several empty validation objects:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/47412359/204756865-2ef0bf84-4762-4591-a875-532adc28cd8d.png)

Since the group summary component only checks if there are any keys present, it will say there are validation errors even though no errors actually exists inside the objects:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/47412359/204758859-6009a436-1f47-48fa-b4c2-8c83a5d47eee.png)
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/47412359/204759085-0f84277e-90bd-43c3-8bf9-971b4b8d219d.png)

Title: Issues with jsonschema validation on app frontend (new datamodels)

Description:
## Description
When XSD has the `xsd:nillable` attribute set, the data model structure becomes 
```json
"oneOf": [
{
  // The actual schema, or reference to it
},
{
  "type": "null"
}
]
```
This is the correct way to set up a schema for a field that is nullable. However it is causing issues in app-frontend validation, since all of the following validation errors are triggered by invalid data against the schema:
- Actual error against the actual schema, f.eks. format, type, etc.
- Error against the second (null) schema
- Error agains the oneOf structure, since it does not "match just one of the schemas exactly".

This results in 3 different error messages in app frontend for the 1 error.

## Screenshots

![Image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1636323/203765826-a8ac1512-78ea-4e11-8f33-c2e961c2f08a.png)

## Solution
We ignore the oneOf validation messages. This is not something that was actually supported properly in app frontend before, so ignoring those messages should not cause any issues. In addition, we ignore the `null` schema error message. We do not have `null` values in form data in app frontend. We only show the validation error on the actual subschema that is failing, which is what is expected in this case.

Title: Single field validation does not run on fields when loading the form

Description:
### Description of the bug

If you're loading existing instance data, fields may appear valid even though [single field validation](https://docs.altinn.studio/app/development/logic/validation/#single-field-validation) would have marked it as invalid. This is because app-frontend will not run single field validation on fields that hasn't been changed in any way - it will just assume validation was successful.

To fix this, we might have to run server-side validation as soon as we load the instance (possibly only if instance data was found).

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Open the `frontend-test` app
2. Type `test` in the first name field, it gives an error
3. Refresh the page, the error is gone until you try to submit the form

### Attempted fix
When fixing #617, I tried fixing this problem at the same time, but my solution was problematic. What I did was extending the saga for `checkIfConditionalRulesShouldRun` to run `FormLayoutActions.updateCurrentView` to update the current view to the current view (hacky!) while telling it to run page validations (and I added a parameter to skip empty field validations). This way validations would run when the page loads (because the saga for `checkIfConditionalRulesShouldRun` runs after the page loads, and after dynamically hidden fields have been hidden when the page loads).

However, this leads to a breaking change (as single field validations can be set up to complain when required data is missing, and running that on the page load is quite user hostile). I found this solution kind-of hacky, so maybe this should be considered in relation to #339 (where we should investigate if we want our app to keep its state after a refresh, or if we can live with an app that behaves differently after a refresh).

Source: https://github.com/Altinn/app-frontend-react/issues/617

Title: Validering kjøres ikke frontend med gyldig json schema

Description:
### Description of the bug

SERES Datamodels (JSON) that were already in Altinn Studio were on the old JSON schema draft. After being edited in the new data models tool, they are converted to 2020-12 compatible. However, the old structure (`properties: { melding: $ref: .. }}`) is still preserved. This is not something our frontend supports, as we have hardcoded the expected structure.

We should change this in app frontend, as we should support _valid_ json schemas even if they are not on the same format as we expect. 
For SERES data models, we have the `melding`-node which contains the schema.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Go to Altinn Studio, find an app with an existing SERES data model.
2. Update the model with a restriction on one of the fields and click Save. Make sure to push changes.
3. Deploy app or run it locally
4. Make a mistake wrt the datamodel to trigger validation error
5. See that client-side validation is not run at all (or at least does not trigger any errors)

### Additional Information

### Solution
I have added a check to support the SERES structure, so that the `info.meldingsnavn` is used as an identifier for the root node. This is a SERES specific node. 
In addition, if `info.rootPath`is set, this is used no matter what other format is there.

Title: Repeating groups: Overflowing table squashes button

Description:
### Description of the bug

In some cases, large tables used for previewing repeating group contents can lead to squashed buttons:

![bug-squashed-button](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/700139/190151935-f2980ba5-cb0a-4234-a57e-4e61cb1dedb1.png)

To a human it's quite obvious that the two columns containing numbers here should get less screen-space, and the title-columns and button-columns should get more (to fill them).

I'll be the first to point out that I've spent a considerable amount of time in a previous project trying to intelligently manage column widths in data tables to make sure content is spaced out to maximize screen real estate - so I would suggest a simpler solution where app developers can control this instead.

### Suggestion 1 (large effort)
It seems to be the case that table headers currently overflow to use multiple lines, making sure to fit all the text. For the table body however, content is cut off with ellipsis when overflowing.

Allow for options to control the width of each column, i.e.:
- A fixed percentage of the full width (i.e. `20%`)
- Non-breaking, use as much space as is needed (default for the button column)
- Divide the rest of the available width equally (this seems to be the default for non-button columns)
- Possibly allow for options to display the full content over multiple lines without ellipsis when overflowing (UX needs to be considered)

### Suggestion 2 (smaller effort)
Make sure the button column is displayed in full. :v: 

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Create a group/table with lots of content
2. Force buttons to have long labels, or cause validation to increase the size of the buttons
3. Observe something similar to the screenshot above

Title: Repeating lists/groups: Entries don't disappear when removed programatically

Description:
### Description of the bug

We are currently trying to populate a repeating list/group based on a choice the user has made previously in the form. The user can then add additional information to these choices previously made in the repeating group.
Populating the list works fine, and is done through DataProsessingHandler. However, removing them does not.

For some reason, the front-end still displays entries that are removed, even though the blob-storage has correctly removed them from the list. And in some cases, it does remove the data from the removed entires, but refills and displays the entry as a copy of one of the actual valid ones. A refresh of the page seems to fix the issue.

What's strange is the fact that the C#-model seems to be remembering the same (wrong) state of the list as the front-end does, even though the blob-storage contains the correct list and values.


### Steps To Reproduce

1. Use an app which populates and depopulates a repeating group based on some previous question in the app.
2. Choose multiple options so as to cause multiple entries to show up in the repeating group
3. See that these show up in the repeating group

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/22012997/177298584-15b6dbda-3d8e-4238-bb8f-e2351c570a60.png)

Title: Specifying an invalid dataModelBinding in layout silently fails

Description:
### Description of the bug

While testing an example app, where the form layout had already been set up, I just spent an annoying amount of time figuring out that a `dataModelBinding` pointing to a non-existing field in the XSD silently fails, and never saves data to the instance data - even though the backend never complains.

### Steps To Reproduce

```xsd
<xsd:complexType name="MyModel">
  <xsd:sequence>
    <xsd:element name="Name" type="xsd:string" />

</xsd:complexType>
```

```json

  "id": "type-your-name",
  "type": "Input",
  "textResourceBindings": {
    "title": "Please type your name"
  },
  "dataModelBindings": {
    "simpleBinding": "MyModel.Naime"
  },
  "required": false
}
```
3. Observe that requests are successful, but no data is actually stored.

Title: WCAG: Parsing

Description:
En samling av feil på kodestruktur som enten er brudd på WCAG eller som ikke følger best practice. 

### Feil plassering av `<style>`
`<style>` Skal ikke være plassert i `<body>`
![Skjermbilde 2022-04-11 kl  08 43 59](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/33222679/162734366-d8e11481-5274-4edb-bef2-c7816852c712.png)
- [x] plasser all `<style>` i `<head>`
-----

### Bruk av prosentverdier i `width` for img
Om man bruker prosenter for å beskrive størrelsen på et bilde skal dette ikke bli lagt i `width` attributtet for `img` elementet. Men heller løses med CSS. [Beskrivelse av feil](https://rocketvalidator.com/html-validation/bad-value-x-for-attribute-width-on-element-img-expected-a-digit-but-saw-instead)
- [x] Når apputvikler bruker prosentverdier blir dette ikke lagt på `width`
-----

### for attributtet peker til en `<div>`
I grupper med radioknapper eller sjekkbokser har vi en label som er plassert i en legend. Denne skal beskrive hele gruppen. I dag så peker **for** attributtet på en` <div> `isteden for en `<input>`. En gruppe med radioknapper eller sjekkbokser vil ha flere input, det kan være man kan peke på flere. Eventuelt så skal man få riktig oppførsel om man legger tekstverdien rett i legend/fieldset som inneholder alle inputer. Da trenger man ikke forholde seg til label/for problematikken. [Eksempel](https://www.accessibility-developer-guide.com/examples/forms/grouping-with-fieldset-legend/#grouping-certain-kind-of-controls)

- [ ] Grupper med radio/sjekkbokser er satt opp riktig

Title: preselectedOptionIndex on checkbox causes unintended selection when navigating in apps

Description:
## Description
The `preselectedOptionIndex` property on checkboxes may cause unintended selections when navigating in an app. For example, if we have a list of optional checkboxes, and we dont want to select any of the options, we can uncheck them all. If the user navigates to next page, and back again, the checkboxes will automatically select the `preselectedOptionIndex` again. 

The user might not notice this and the form will be submitted with incorrect information.

## To Reproduce
(app with repro: https://dev.altinn.studio/repos/haakemon/ui-components/src/branch/bug-checkbox-multi-pages-initial-value )
1. Create a app with 2 pages
2. Add checkboxes on page 1, and set a `preselectedOptionIndex`.
3. Start the app, and go to page 1. Untick all checkboxes
4. Navigate to page 2
5. Navigate back to page 1, observe the checkbox will now have selected the default value again

There is an additional bug with checkboxes and preselectedOptionIndex, where you are currently unable to deselect that checkbox at all, since on every render, it will select the checkbox automatically. This is being fixed as part of Altinn/altinn-studio#7464

## Expected behavior
The checkbox should not select the default value when navigating back

## Additional info
I'm not sure if theres any good way to solve this, or if its possible to solve at all with the current architecture.

No production apps (as [per this list in November 2021](https://docs.altinn.studio/app/launched-apps/)) are using this property, so we could consider to remove it entirely. This property also does not cover all usecases, f.ex you cannot have multiple preselected values.

App authors can anyway solve the preselecting of data by setting the form data to the wanted values during instantiation, or prefill.

Title: Prefix/suffix in input fields should have language support + way to differentiate thousand/decimal based on language

Description:
## What needs to be solved?
There doesn't seem to be a way to get correct thousand separator depending on the chosen language (and probably also for the decimal separator) for numbers in input fields. The normal way to write large decimal numbers is f.ex. 1 000 000,00 in Norwegian and 1,000,000.00 in English.

## How do you want it solved?
The easiest would be that the browser "discovers" that it is a number and formats it automatically. We need to be able to specify the number of decimals somewhere. Maybe the best way to do this is with css, which you say you "don't support"? Supporting a "prefix" depending on the chosen language is probably impossible with css.

## Alternative solutions
You could improve the functionality for the Input-field by expanding the options for this type of element: 

{
  "id": "numberComponent",
  "type": "Input",
  ...
  "formatting": {
    "number": {
      "thousandSeparator": " ",
      "prefix": "kr "
    },
    "align":"right"
  }
},

The parameter "thousandSeparator" would have solved the problem if it were possible to use an **id** from the json-language-files to define if it should be space or decimal. You would then also need a similar parameter for "decimalPoint" with language support. The "prefix" should also have the possibility of referring to an id in the json-language-files.

The number of decimals should also be an option under "number" (maybe it already is?)

## Additional context
This feature is connected to the description in the documentation here: https://docs.altinn.studio/nb/app/development/ux/styling/#:~:text=Formattert%20tall%20i%20input%2Dfelt

Title: New instance is created when unauthenticated user accesses instance via direct link

Description:
## Describe the bug
If a user bookmarks an instance, and goes directly to this link to work on the form withough being logged in, a new instance is created, rather than the user having to authenticate themselves and then being returned to the existing instance. 


## To Reproduce
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Go to https://ttd.apps.tt02.altinn.no/ttd/apps-test
2. Log on and start filling out form
3. Save url
4. Log out of altinn
5. Access url directly 
6. Log on with same test user
7. See error

## Expected behavior
User has to log in and is then redirected to the initial instance. 

## Analysis
When pasting direct url in browser e.g. http://altinn3local.no/ttd/apps-test/#/instance/512345/3b11f912-1a00-478e-bf77-df4ae6f615f2
The request found in the network log is: http://altinn3local.no/ttd/apps-test/

We need to reconsider the route to the endpoint that returns the frontend view. Changing # for `display` or another string fixes the problem, so we need a character that is forwarded by the browser to the server. `#` is not a valid character.

Alternatively, browser-routes could be used by app frontend instead.

note that redirect url in backend should be defined as

```cs
    string goToUrl = HttpUtility.UrlEncode($"{scheme}://{Request.Host}{Request.Path}");
```
 including query parameters could also be considered here. 

## Browser router instead of hash-router
The issue has come from the fact that we use [hash-router](https://reactrouter.com/web/api/HashRouter) as the routing tool in our SPA. An option here would instead be to use [browser-router](https://reactrouter.com/web/api/BrowserRouter) which actually uses the HTML5 history API (pushState, replaceState and the popstate event) to keep your UI in sync with the URL. This would solve the issue of having the full url in backend when doing the redirect.

Some questions that do arise:
- How can we be backward compatible? Old urls that contain `#` no longer work 
  - Redirect old urls in frontend?
- How does message-box link? Do we have any apps that run on v2 of app frontend? These would break.
- For all possible url's we would want in app frontend in the future, these url's should return the SPA from backend. Is this an issue?

## Tasks
- [ ] POC possible solutions
  - [ ] browser router (or other routers that use html 5 api)
  - [ ] app-frontend is responsible for handling 401-responses
    - [ ] extend the refresh-token logic in app-frontend? 
- [ ] Fix routes for app frontend
- [ ] Add additional route for HomeController in AppTemplate to also accept and forward requests towards old org/app/#/instances/{instanceOwnerPartyId}/{instanceGuid} endpoint. 
- [ ] Do we need to update string template for instance url in messagebox? When can this be done?
- [ ] Regression tests

Title: JSON-schema validation frontend can't handle restrictions with nested base references

Description:
## Describe the bug
Our json-schema validation in app frontend does not respect a nested element restriction. 

The base xsd:
```
<xsd:schema xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema">
    <xsd:simpleType name="Tekst">
        <xsd:restriction base="xsd:string">
            <xsd:maxLength value="4000"/>
        </xsd:restriction>
    </xsd:simpleType>
    <xsd:simpleType name="Organisasjonsnummer">
        <xsd:restriction base="Tekst">
            <xsd:pattern value="[0-9]+"/>
            <xsd:length value="9"/>
        </xsd:restriction>
    </xsd:simpleType>
</xsd:schema>
```

Here the simple type Organisasjonsnummer references the simple type `Tekst` as its restriction base, which in turn references `xsd:string`. 

In our validation app frontend only the simple type `Tekst` is respected, and validations that are defined within `Organisasjonsnummer` are ignored.

We have to look into if there is an issue with the generated JSON-schema, or if we are doing something wrong while validating frontend. 

## Analysis

This does indeed seem to be a problem with our frontend json-schema validation. Given the he following JSON schema:
```
{
  "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/schema#",
  "$id": "schema.json",
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "Skjema": {
      "$ref": "#/definitions/Skjema"
    }
  },
  "definitions": {
    "Skjema": {
      "properties": {
        "person": {
          "type": "object",
          "properties": {
            "age": {
              "type": "integer",
              "minimum": 0,
              "maximum": 100
            }
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

If you here try to validate the field Skjema.person.age with the value "1" you get a type error, as this is validated against the "type": object from the parent definition... 

The frontend issue is fixed in Altinn/altinn-studio#6855. Nested restrictions in xsd does still generate invalid json-schemas, this needs to be re-tested when new datamodelling tool is complete.

## To Reproduce
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Upload a data model with nested restrictions
2. See that app frontend ignores all other validations than the first base

## Expected behavior
As the xml-spec states that the base class as:

> Required. Specifies the name of a built-in data type, simpleType element, or complexType element defined in this schema or another schema

We should support referencing simpleTypes and complexTypes as the base for a restriction.

Title: File uploader – undefined filetypes

Description:
## Describe the bug
If the service developer has chosen to define which filetypes that can be uploaded, but then hasn't typed in anything. the filetype is set to undefined and that is what is shown to the end user, which doesn't mean anything.

## To Reproduce
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Create a new service or go to an existing one
2. Go to ui editor and drag in a file uploader
3. check the "egendefinerte filtyper" radiobutton
4. Go to test and create a new instance
5. See that the allowed file types are set to "undefined"
3. See error

## Expected behavior
That all file types are still allowed and undefined is not shown to the end user. To the end user in Altinn it should look and behave the same as for when the "egendefinerte filtyper" is not checked.

## Screenshots
![Screenshot 2019-05-16 at 16 45 32](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/6996124/57863739-e8a27100-77fa-11e9-90c9-c160562b27bf.png)


## Additional info
Tested in altinn.studio

## Fix
If they don't write anything, every filetype is allowed. This must be reflected in the application the same way as if they choose every filetype in the UI-editor. "alle" written after "tillatte filformater:" in the component. 

## Acceptance criterea 
- When the there are no values in the "skriv in gyldige filtyper" field, the component should act as if "Alle filtyper" is selected. 
- The component should tell the end-user that all filetypes are allowed.
